title: On the $O(1/T)$ Convergence of Alternating Gradient Descent–Ascent in Bilinear Games
claim: Optimizing stepsizes shows the alternating method attains a markedly lower worst-case error and faster decay with horizon than its simultaneous counterpart.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter plots sharing legend, labeled (a)/(b), log-log on right
description: Two side-by-side scatter plots comparing AltGDA (blue circles) with SimGDA (orange diamonds) across horizon T from 5 to 50. Panel (a), titled 'Optimized Step Size vs T', plots the optimized stepsize η on a linear axis. AltGDA stays near 1.2 to 1.6 with a slight sawtooth pattern. SimGDA starts near 2.0 and falls below 0.5, with a visible jump around T=27. Panel (b), titled 'Optimized Objective Value vs T', uses log-log axes for the worst-case duality gap. AltGDA sits well below SimGDA and falls more steeply, so the gap between the two grows with T. Both panels have a boxed legend at top right. Captions (a) and (b) sit below. The eye goes first to the widely separated blue and orange point sequences in (b).
caption: Optimized stepsizes and corresponding optimized objective values for T = 5, 6, . . . , 50 via PEP. The left plot shows the optimized stepsizes. The optimized objective value in the right plot denotes the worst-case performance measure (i.e., duality gap of the averaged iterates) corresponding to the optimized stepsizes on log scale.
abstract: We study the alternating gradient descent-ascent (AltGDA) algorithm in two-player zero-sum games. Alternating methods, where players take turns to update their strategies, have long been recognized as simple and practical approaches for learning in games, exhibiting much better numerical performance than their simultaneous counterparts. However, our theoretical understanding of alternating algorithms remains limited, and results are mostly restricted to the unconstrained setting. We show that for two-player zero-sum games that admit an interior Nash equilibrium, AltGDA converges at an $O(1/T)$ ergodic convergence rate when employing a small constant stepsize. This is the first result showing that alternation improves over the simultaneous counterpart of GDA in the constrained setting. For games without an interior equilibrium, we show an $O(1/T)$ local convergence rate with a constant stepsize that is independent of any game-specific constants. In a more general setting, we develop a performance estimation programming (PEP) framework to jointly optimize the AltGDA stepsize along with its worst-case convergence rate. The PEP results indicate that AltGDA may achieve an $O(1/T)$ convergence rate for a finite horizon $T$, whereas its simultaneous counterpart appears limited to an $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ rate.
